lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's use OOP to model a complicated object, like a car. When we drive a car, we don't need to understand its inner mechanics.

Similarly, when working with code, we want to understand the core methods without being bogged down by details.

lessons.title: Real objects have many functions
lessons.interactiveContent:
A car does a lot of things at the same time. For example, a car injects and ignites fuel thousands of times a minute just to stay running.

Make sure to pick "Spraying fuel" followed by ) and then (, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
A car does a lot of things at the same time. For example, a car injects and ignites fuel thousands of times a minute just to stay running.

Make injectFuel print Spraying fuel and igniteFuel print Boom!.

Make sure to pick print, followed by "Spraying fuel", print, and finally "Boom!".

lessons.title: OOP without abstraction is hard to use
lessons.interactiveContent: Modeling a car in Python works the same. However, repeatedly calling methods can make it harder to read and use.

lessons.title: OOP without abstraction can lead to bugs
lessons.interactiveContent:
Besides that, managing each individual method call by ourselves increases the chance we'll make a mistake and cause unwanted effects.

Make sure to pick car.injectFuel().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Besides that, managing each individual method call by ourselves increases the chance we'll make a mistake and cause unwanted effects.

Spray fuel a second time before igniting, so the console shows Spraying fuel twice, then Boom!.

Make sure to pick car.injectFuel().

lessons.title: Abstraction 1
lessons.interactiveContent: Cars do all of this low-level functionality for us, and we only have to start them up. Hiding these details is called abstraction.

lessons.title: Abstraction 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
We implement abstraction in OOP by writing a few core functions that handle all of the low-level work.

Make sure to pick startUp(self).
lessons.hardModeContent:
We implement abstraction in OOP by writing a few core functions that handle all of the low-level work.

Finish startUp so that while the car is on it keeps injecting, then igniting fuel.

Make sure to pick startUp, followed by self.on, injectFuel, and finally igniteFuel.

lessons.title: Abstraction 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Abstraction allows other developers to use a class without having to know what low-level methods it has or how they even work.

Make sure to pick Car, followed by (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Abstraction 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Other developers can create a new object from our Car class and use it by just calling a few core methods.

Make sure to pick startUp, followed by (, and finally ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Other developers can create a new object from our Car class and use it by just calling a few core methods.

On the second line, build the full call that starts the car with its one core method, not the low-level ones.

Make sure to pick car, followed by ., startUp, (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is abstraction?

Simplifying how we interact with objects down to a few methodsReducing the total number of methods objects have

Simplifying how we interact with objects down to a few methods.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Abstraction simplifies how we interact with objects down to a few methods.

Which music player design uses abstraction?

A play() method handles connecting, decoding, and producing soundEvery low-level operation must be called separately by the userThe player removes all low-level operations so it has fewer methods

A play() method handles connecting, decoding, and producing sound.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we implement abstraction?

Write a few core methods that handle low-level functionsBy making all low-level methods available for other developers to call

Write a few core methods that handle low-level functions.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We implement abstraction with a few core methods that handle low-level functions.

How should a thermostat let developers choose a target temperature?

Expose set_temperature() and let it handle heating or coolingRequire developers to call every heating and cooling step directlyDelete the low-level functions instead of handling them

Expose set_temperature() and let it handle heating or cooling.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why is implementing abstraction important?

So others can use a class without knowing how it worksSo others know how a class works only after testing it

So others can use a class without knowing how it works.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Abstraction lets others use a class without knowing how it works.

A developer calls charge() without knowing its encryption and network steps. Why is that useful?

The developer can use the payment class through its core methodThe developer must test each hidden step to discover how the class worksThe developer must rewrite the hidden steps before calling the class

The developer can use the payment class through its core method.

lessons.title: Question 4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is one of the benefits of abstraction?

Fewer bugs caused by user errorUsers have more direct control over an object's behavior

Fewer bugs caused by user error.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A coffee machine offers brew() instead of exposing separate heater, pump, and valve controls.

Which benefit does this abstraction provide?

It reduces bugs caused by users calling low-level operations incorrectlyIt gives users more direct control over every internal operationIt guarantees that the internal code can never contain a bug

It reduces bugs caused by users calling low-level operations incorrectly.

lessons.title: Question 5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these could be a core method for a camera?

take_photo()close_shutter()

Make sure to pick take_photo().
lessons.hardModeContent:
A camera should offer one method for the user's main goal while handling shutter and sensor details internally.

Which method should be the core method?

take_photo()close_shutter()read_sensor_voltage()

Make sure to pick take_photo().

lessons.title: Example 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Abstract this class by creating a makeCoffee() method that heats water, adds it to coffee grounds, and filters off the coffee.

Make sure to pick makeCoffee(self) followed by self and then brew, self.filterCoffee().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Abstract this class by creating a makeCoffee() method that heats water, adds it to coffee grounds, and filters off the coffee.

Have makeCoffee heat the water, then brew, then filter, so the console shows those three steps in order.

Make sure to pick heatWater, followed by brew, filterCoffee, and finally makeCoffee.

lessons.hardModeContent:
To make ice cream, we must both churn and freeze cream. Call the method of iceCreamMaker that does both for us.

Fill in the two steps inside makeIceCream, then build the call, so the console shows Churning cream then Freezing cream.

Make sure to pick self.churn(), followed by self.freeze(), iceCreamMaker, ., makeIceCream, (, and finally ).
